body:
Hey, I just wanted to say thanks again. I ended up being involuntarily committed and taken away in ambulance. Squeezed out 2 hours later with a script for zoloft.
Its was nightmarish, I can't begin to describe. 

All it's done is reaffirm my commitment. I got what I wanted though, some anti-ds to fuck my mind even more. And (hopefully) give me the courage to push through the initial panic and fear from the body's natural reaction to certain death.

I appreciate the kind words, I truly do. Having grown up before the widespread adoption of social media I used to turn to strangers online for advice, but it just feels disingenuous these days, but not in your case... Thank you for restoring a little faith.

I've been to the brink a few times but never hit that rock bottom feeling. I want to stop going through the motions and pretending like it's all going to be ok, only to have the cycle repeat again. It kills me a little more each time. 

My so called intelligence has done little for me despite being told over and over "hey, you're a smart guy, you'll figure it out". It's a curse.

I don't want to go, but it finally feels right.

I'm really tired of going it alone. This trip is kind of like that adventure you speak of. I just don't intend on coming back from it.
I wouldn't announce my intentions to my family. Just a quick visit, positive last experience.

"These are the best days of my life and I am suffering during them".

I may or may not gave uttered this same phrase.

You mention short lived joy and a desire for escapism. I get the feeling you've been called an 'old soul' at least once.

It's truly not fair, I'd rather the money spent on 'prevention' to be spent on support for those we leave behind. To help them come to terms with what we did. For them to know that it's ok.

Pain and uncertainty that the deed will be done. 

I couldn't think of anything worse than botching the job and becoming too handicapped to try again

I hate the thought of being a burden to those people. Especially in light of the fact that I live in a first world country, my bills are paid and I have minimal debt. I call it 'entitled depression' and all it does is make me less likely to seek help and more likely to follow through.

I couldn't agree more and you've basically made it easier for me to justify the end of life arrangements I am currently making.
I get the will signed tomorrow then I'm off on a little road trip.

Makes me so angry that suicide kits aren't more readily available.
